n: President Joseph F. Smith, sixth President of the Church and nephew of Joseph Smith, received this vision on October 3, 1918, about six weeks before his death. That year he had lost his son Hyrum Mack Smith, and the world was suffering from World War I and the influenza pandemic. He begins quietly, pondering scripture in his room.
He was reflecting on Christ’s atoning sacrifice for the redemption of the world.
He marveled at the love shown by both the Father and the Son in sending the Redeemer.
Through Christ’s Atonement and obedience to gospel principles, all humankind can be saved.

f.w: by obedience to the principles of the gospel

n: His thoughts turned to Peter’s letters to early Christians scattered across Asia Minor (modern Turkey).
Reading 1 Peter 3 and 4, he was struck more deeply than ever by certain passages.

f.w: the third and fourth chapters of the first epistle of Peter

n: Peter teaches that Christ, the just, suffered once for the unjust to bring us to God; he died in the flesh but was made alive by the Spirit.
Between death and resurrection, Christ went and preached to the spirits in prison.

f.w: preached unto the spirits in prison

n: These spirits had been disobedient in Noah’s day, when only eight people were saved in the ark.

f.w: eight souls were saved by water

n: The gospel was preached to the dead so they could be judged fairly, as people in the flesh are, and live spiritually with God.

f.w: the gospel preached also to them that are dead

n: As he pondered, his spiritual eyes opened, and he saw the vast host of the dead.

f.w: the eyes of my understanding were opened

n: Gathered in one place were countless righteous spirits who had been faithful to Jesus’ testimony in life.
They had offered sacrifices symbolizing Christ’s great sacrifice and suffered for his name.

f.w: in the similitude of the great sacrifice

n: They had died firm in the hope of a glorious resurrection through God’s grace.

f.w: firm in the hope of a glorious resurrection

n: They were joyful, because their day of deliverance was near.
They waited for the Son of God to come into the spirit world to announce their redemption from death.
Their bodies would be restored perfectly—bone to bone, sinew and flesh—spirit and body united forever for a fulness of joy.
While they waited, the Son of God appeared, proclaiming liberty to the faithful captives.
He taught them the gospel, the resurrection, and redemption from the Fall and from personal sins through repentance.
He did not go personally to the wicked who had defiled themselves.

f.w: unto the wicked he did not go
f.g: This clarifies how Peter’s words in 1 Peter 3:19 were carried out.

n: The rebellious who rejected ancient prophets did not see his face.
Where they were, darkness reigned; among the righteous was peace.

f.w: among the righteous there was peace

n: The righteous rejoiced, knelt, and acknowledged Christ as their Redeemer and Deliverer.
Their faces shone with the Lord’s radiance, and they sang his praises.
President Smith marveled that Jesus had spent about three years teaching in mortality.

f.g: The length of Jesus’ mortal ministry is traditionally estimated from the Passovers mentioned in John.

n: Yet despite his miracles and teaching, few accepted him.

f.w: there were but few who hearkened

n: His ministry among the dead lasted only from his crucifixion to his resurrection—parts of three days.

f.g: Roughly from Friday afternoon to Sunday morning.

n: He wondered how Christ could preach to all the disobedient spirits in so short a time.

f.g: An honest question that leads to revelation.

n: His understanding opened: the Lord did not personally go among the wicked.
Instead, he organized the righteous spirits into a missionary force, gave them power and authority, and sent them to carry the gospel to all spirits in darkness.

f.w: he organized his forces and appointed messengers

n: The messengers proclaimed liberty to all willing to repent and receive the gospel.

f.w: the acceptable day of the Lord

n: Thus the gospel reached those who died in sin, in ignorance, or after rejecting the prophets.

f.w: without a knowledge of the truth

n: They were taught faith, repentance, vicarious (proxy) baptism, and the gift of the Holy Ghost—the first principles of the gospel.

f.g: Baptism performed by a living person on behalf of someone who has died.

f.w: faith in God, repentance from sin

n: And all other principles needed to be judged fairly and live with God in the spirit.

f.w: judged according to men in the flesh

n: Thus all the dead learned that redemption came through Christ’s sacrifice on the cross.
The Redeemer spent his time in the spirit world preparing the faithful prophets who had testified of him.
They would carry his message to all the dead he could not visit personally because of their rebellion.
Among the great assembly was Adam, the Ancient of Days, father of all.
Also “our glorious Mother Eve,” with many faithful daughters through the ages. This verse affirms the place of righteous women in God’s work.
Abel, the first martyr, and Seth, who looked just like his father Adam.

f.w: the express image of his father

n: Noah, Shem, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Moses the lawgiver.

f.w: Abraham, the father of the faithful

n: Isaiah, who prophesied the Redeemer would heal the brokenhearted and open the prison to the bound.
Ezekiel, who saw the valley of dry bones come back to life—a symbol of the resurrection.

f.w: the great valley of dry bones

n: Daniel, who foresaw God’s latter-day kingdom that would never be destroyed.
Elias, who was with Moses on the Mount of Transfiguration.
Malachi, who prophesied Elijah’s coming—a prophecy Moroni repeated to Joseph Smith.
Elijah would plant in children’s hearts the promises made to the fathers.

f.w: plant in the hearts of the children the promises made to their fathers

n: This foreshadowed temple work for the dead and the sealing of families, without which the earth would be wasted at Christ’s coming.

f.w: the sealing of the children to their parents

n: Nephite prophets who testified of Christ were also there, awaiting deliverance.

f.w: the prophets who dwelt among the Nephites

n: The dead viewed the separation of spirit from body as a kind of bondage.
Christ taught them and gave them power to rise after his resurrection and enter the Father’s kingdom.

f.w: to come forth, after his resurrection

n: They would continue their labors and share every blessing reserved for those who love God.

f.w: held in reserve for them that love him

n: President Smith also saw Joseph Smith, his own father Hyrum, Brigham Young, John Taylor, Wilford Woodruff, and others reserved to lay the foundation of the latter-day work.

f.g: Joseph F. Smith was five when his father Hyrum was martyred in 1844.

n: Their work included building temples and performing ordinances for the dead.
They were among the “noble and great ones” chosen before birth to lead.
Before birth they received their first lessons in the spirit world and were prepared to labor in God’s vineyard.

f.w: received their first lessons in the world of spirits

n: Faithful elders who die continue preaching the gospel in the spirit world. Missionary work goes on after death.
The dead who repent will be redeemed through temple ordinances performed for them.

f.w: ordinances of the house of God

n: After paying for their sins and being washed clean, they receive a reward according to their works as heirs of salvation.
President Smith bears testimony that the vision is true. It was accepted as scripture in 1976 and added to the Doctrine and Covenants in 1981.

f.w: I know that this record is true
